subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should the layered Tailscale-plus-shared-secret contract ship, and should tokenless Tailscale sessions intentionally be invalidated by ordinary token/password rotations as well as policy toggles?
rationale: This creates a new Gateway security/config contract, while the generation reuse introduces an availability and compatibility tradeoff not established by current behavior.

options.title: Separate Policy Generation
options.body: Approve layered auth but track its Tailscale policy independently so only relevant policy changes invalidate tokenless sessions.

options.title: Accept Coupled Invalidation
options.body: Approve the current generation reuse and explicitly document that shared-secret rotation also disconnects tokenless Tailscale sessions.

options.title: Decline Layered Auth
options.body: Keep the existing separate Tailscale-identity and explicit shared-secret deployment paths.

recommendation.title: Separate Policy Generation
recommendation.body: Approve layered auth but track its Tailscale policy independently so only relevant policy changes invalidate tokenless sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway authentication and security work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the boundary decision.
